prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1449; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's policy holder reporting a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the submitted photographs, which confirm the general location of the vehicles and the front-end damage described in the report. No independent witnesses have been identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Estimate review completed. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact, and the repair scope appears consistent with the photos. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claim history.

Entry 4: Coverage verification confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start. Policy status is active on the loss date.

Entry 5: Recorded statement from the claimant, through counsel, describes the collision. The claimant gave the same account in every conversation so far. Seating position in the vehicle at impact is still not fully clear from the statements and will need follow-up.

Entry 6: Medical records received showing a neck strain. The injury matches the kind and force of the crash well, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.

Entry 7: File reviewed and referred for evaluation of the bodily injury component. Open item: confirm seating position with counsel before the injury evaluation is finalized.
